Backend: 15/15 PASS (/app/backend/tests/test_devices_iter16.py, junit at /app/test_reports/pytest/iter16_devices.xml). Verified: (a) Known-device login path (qa-device-1 pre-registered via /auth/device/touch) — no email sent, no 'Yeni cihaz e-postası gönderilemedi' error in supervisor logs. (b) /auth/device/touch silently inserts unknown device without triggering email. (c) GET /auth/devices returns only caller's own rows; exactly one row has current=true (matches X-Device-Id header); device_id is stripped from response. (d) DELETE /auth/devices/{id}: Özkan deleting Murat's row → 404; Murat deleting own row → 200 and row removed from DB. (e) POST /auth/logout-all bumps token_version; prior token immediately returns 401 on /auth/me; re-login works. (f) POST /admin/users/{murat_id}/logout: Murat (role=user) → 403; Özkan on self → 400; Özkan on Murat → 200 and Murat's prior token 401. (g) GET /admin/users returns last_active_at, device_count, last_device (browser/os/last_seen) for every row. (h) SINGLE new-device test: Murat login with qa-device-2 (sends 1 email each to Murat + Özkan as allowed) succeeded; qa-device-2 persisted in db.user_devices; no error logs. (i) Regression: /sales /tires /cariler /incomes /expenses /sampiyon/history all 200 for Murat (confirms get_current_user Request param addition is backward-compatible). (j) /auth/forgot-password with unregistered email → 404 (unchanged). Frontend (Playwright, viewport 1920x1080, device_id locked to qa-device-1 in localStorage before every login): Murat → Ayarlar dialog shows devices-section with 'Bu cihaz' badge on the only row (Chrome · Linux), logout-all-btn visible, user-management HIDDEN (correct). Özkan → user-management shown with 2 rows (Murat tagged '● Şu an aktif · Chrome · Linux · 1 cihaz' + admin-user-logout button; Özkan row '(siz) Yönetici' with ONLY edit button, logout button correctly ABSENT). SettingsDialog opens with admin UX including Devices + ChangePassword + UserManagement sections. Dashboard/Satışlar/Stok/Cariler all render without errors. Cleanup: at end deleted ALL qa-* rows from db.user_devices and purged login_attempts for the test emails — DB verified empty of test artifacts. No real-account data modified (name/email/password unchanged). Admin-triggered 30s poll invalidation (Murat auto-redirect to /login after admin logout) was NOT directly exercised in UI because it requires two live browser contexts simultaneously, but the underlying mechanic is backend-verified in test_admin_force_logout_matrix (token_version bump → old token 401 → axios interceptor redirects to /login).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _touch_device uses a MODULE-LEVEL dict _DEVICE_TOUCH as a rate-limit cache (60s). This leaks memory over time (key per user+device pair, never evicted) and is not safe across multi-worker uvicorn deployments — each worker has its own cache, so one user hitting worker A then worker B triggers two DB writes per minute. Fine for current single-worker preview; add TTL eviction or move to Redis before scaling.

AuthContext.jsx 30s poll only invokes api.get('/auth/me') and relies on axios interceptor to redirect on 401. That works, but if the server returns any 401 (e.g., transient DB blip) the user is force-logged-out immediately. Consider requiring 2 consecutive 401s before redirect, or distinguish 'Oturum sonlandırıldı' from other 401s.

Devices.jsx logoutAll(): on success it calls both localStorage.removeItem('ks_token') AND logout() (which also removes the token and POSTs /auth/logout). The second call will fail silently (401 from invalidated token) — functionally fine but produces an extra noisy error in network tab. Just call logout() alone.
server.py admin_force_logout: no notification to the affected user. Consider logging an 'oturumunuz yönetici tarafından kapatıldı' entry visible in UI next login.

server.py _register_login_device: first_ever check is based on count_documents > 0, which is race-prone if two logins happen simultaneously on different brand-new devices (both could skip the email because insert_one is between the count and the task spawn). Low probability; acceptable.
